title: Root maps and pinning rigidity for an existing quasi-finite surjection
statement:
Let $A$ be a nonzero commutative ring and $(G_i,T_i=D_A(M_i))$, $i=0,1$, split realizations with reduced root data $(M_i,\Phi_i,M_i^\vee,\Phi_i^\vee)$ [def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization]. Suppose $h:M_0\hookrightarrow M_1$ has finite cokernel, $b:\Phi_1\to\Phi_0$ is a bijection, $h(b(\alpha))=\alpha$ and $h^\vee(\alpha^\vee)=b(\alpha)^\vee$ for every root. Let $g:G_1\to G_0$ be a quasi-finite surjective homomorphism restricting to $D_A(h)$ [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group]; quasi-finite means finite type with finite fibres as topological spaces.

For a generator $X$ of a root module $\mathfrak g_{i,\gamma}$, there is a unique $T_i$-equivariant closed group homomorphism $x_{i,\gamma,X}:\mathbf G_{a,A}\to G_i$ with differential $1\mapsto X$, where $\mathbf G_{a,A}(B)=(B,+)$ and $t\in T_i(B)$ acts on $B$ by multiplication by $\gamma(t)$. It parametrizes the $\gamma$-root subgroup. For any generators $X$ of $\mathfrak g_{1,\alpha}$ and $Y$ of $\mathfrak g_{0,b(\alpha)}$, there is a unit $a_\alpha\in A^\times$ such that $g(x_{1,\alpha,X}(z))=x_{0,b(\alpha),Y}(a_\alpha z)$ for every $A$-algebra and every $z$ in it, and $dg(X)=a_\alpha Y$. All these assertions commute with arbitrary ring base change. Finally choose bases with $b(\Delta_1)=\Delta_0$. If two such quasi-finite surjective homomorphisms have the same torus restriction and agree on each chosen simple-root tangent generator for $\Delta_1$, they are equal as $A$-group-scheme morphisms. The base ring may be disconnected or nonreduced.

source.place: Theorem 4.1.4 (canonical root groups), Lemma 6.1.4, printed pp.188--189, with all root exponents one, and Proposition 6.1.13(2), pp.194--195. The latter is uniqueness for an already given quasi-finite surjection, not existence of an isogeny. Read online; local PDF WANTED. No Stacks tag states this reductive-group theorem.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-split-reductive-finite-diagram-model] to the two given split realizations, choosing generators of their finitely many free root modules, and to $g$ as a marked arrow. For the uniqueness assertion include both arrows and the equalities of their simple-root differentials. The resulting $A_0\subseteq A$ is Noetherian and retains the fixed lattices, roots, coroots, torus maps, generators and quasi-finiteness hypotheses. We first construct and prove the assertions over a Noetherian ring $R$, locally on its spectrum when a cited result requires $R$ local. Later steps prove uniqueness and base-change compatibility, so local constructions glue and can be pulled back from $A_0$ to $A$. No reduction of $A$ or passage merely to its geometric points is used. For $R\to R_{\mathfrak p}$, finite type follows by localizing a finite generating set, and every fibre of the localized map is a fibre of the original map with the same residue field. Thus the finite-fibre hypothesis is retained in the local arguments.

source.place: Corollary 3.1.11 and Lemma 3.2.5, pp.88-93; finite-data reduction preceding Lemma 6.1.4.

proof.text: For either split realization over the Noetherian ring $R$, apply [lem-sfb-relative-canonical-root-exponential] to its root line. Composing $\exp_\gamma$ with $z\mapsto zX$ gives the closed homomorphism $x_{i,\gamma,X}$ with the required equivariance and differential. Any other such equivariant homomorphism gives, by the inverse identification $R\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathfrak g_{i,\gamma}$, another homomorphism from the root vector group with the same tangent inclusion; the uniqueness clause of the cited node makes it equal. Its image is the root subgroup on every geometric fibre, and the closed image is its canonical relative root subgroup. The cited construction is compatible with arbitrary base change.

Fix $\alpha\in\Phi_1$ and put $\beta=b(\alpha)$. In $M_i$ let $L_1=M_1\cap\mathbf Q\alpha$ and $L_0=M_0\cap\mathbf Q\beta$. Because $h_{\mathbf Q}$ is an isomorphism and $h(\beta)=\alpha$, $h^{-1}(L_1)=L_0$. Thus $M_0/L_0\to M_1/L_1$ is injective with finite cokernel. By [lem-sfb-relative-diagonalizable-character-duality], $g$ maps the root-kernel torus $T_{1,\alpha}=D_R(M_1/L_1)$ onto $T_{0,\beta}=D_R(M_0/L_0)$ as an fppf sheaf. Form the smooth reductive rank-one centralizers $H_i$ of these tori using [lem-sfb-relative-root-rank-one-centralizer]. If $v$ centralizes $T_{1,\alpha}$, then $g(v)$ centralizes every locally lifted point of $T_{0,\beta}$, hence every point of it: equality of points of an affine scheme can be checked after a faithfully flat extension. This gives a homomorphism $H_1\to H_0$, on all test algebras, rather than just a containment of geometric images.

The relation $h^\vee(\alpha^\vee)=\beta^\vee$ makes $H_1\to H_0$ equivariant for conjugation by these coroots. The attracting subgroup in $H_i$ for its positive coroot is its positive root subgroup. The hypotheses of [lem-sfb-relative-rank-one-local-matrix-model] hold for $(H_i,T_i)$ over each Noetherian local base: by the base-change clause of [lem-sfb-relative-root-rank-one-centralizer], each geometric fibre of $H_i$ is the centralizer of the fibre of $T_{i,\alpha}=\ker\chi_{\alpha_0}$, which is the largest subtorus of $\ker\chi_\alpha$ (that kernel is $\mu_d\times\mathbf G_m^{r-1}$ and a torus has no nontrivial map to $\mu_d$), so it is reductive of semisimple rank one by [lem-sfb-reductive-rank-one-reflections]; its roots are $\pm\alpha$ and $T_i$ is a maximal torus of it. Here this identification can be checked over the local matrix charts of [lem-sfb-relative-rank-one-local-matrix-model]: in $\mathrm{SL}_2$ or $\mathrm{GL}_2$, conjugation by $\operatorname{diag}(t,t^{-1})$ contracts exactly the upper unitriangular matrices; its diagonal is fixed and the lower entry has weight $-2$. The same computation in the scalar quotient gives the assertion for $\mathrm{PGL}_2$; central torus factors are fixed and so their contracted points equal $1$. The coroot is the indicated diagonal cocharacter, since this holds on geometric fibres and the split-torus equality criterion in [lem-sfb-relative-diagonalizable-character-duality] identifies the cocharacters. Consequently functoriality of attracting subgroups in [lem-sfb-relative-dynamic-attracting-subgroup] gives $g(U_{1,\alpha})\subseteq U_{0,\beta}$ scheme-theoretically. The same argument applies to negative roots.

source.place: Lemma 6.1.4, p.188, with Theorem 5.1.8, pp.139-140, and Proposition 4.1.10(2).

proof.text:
In the chosen root coordinates write $g(x_{1,\alpha,X}(z))=x_{0,\beta,Y}(P(z))$, where $P\in R[z]$ and $P(0)=0$. Full $T_1$-equivariance, and $h(\beta)=\alpha$, give the coefficient identity
$$\sum_j c_j z^j e^{j\alpha}=\sum_j c_j z^j e^\alpha\quad\text{in }R[M_1][z],\qquad P(z)=\sum_jc_jz^j.$$
The monomials $e^m$ form an $R$-basis of $R[M_1]$ by [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group]; $j\alpha=\alpha$ implies $j=1$ since $M_1$ is torsion free and $\alpha\ne0$. Thus $P(z)=c z$, even when $R$ has nilpotents. If $c$ lay in a maximal ideal, reduction to its residue field would put the entire embedded affine-line root subgroup in a fibre of $g$, contradicting the finite-fibre hypothesis. Hence $c\in R^\times$. Differentiating on $z=\epsilon$ gives $dg(X)=cY$. The coordinate identity also proves uniqueness of $c$.

source.place: Lemma 6.1.4, second paragraph of proof, p.189; exponent-one coefficient comparison.

proof.text:
For the rigidity calculation choose opposite generators normalized as follows. Inside each rank-one centralizer take the upper and lower matrix parametrizations of [lem-sfb-relative-rank-one-local-matrix-model], scaled reciprocally to give the prescribed positive generator. They are the canonical root maps by step 2. Matrix multiplication gives, with $w=1+uv$ invertible,
$$x_+(u)x_-(v)=x_-(v/w)\,\gamma^\vee(w)\,x_+(u/w).$$
The formula is unchanged in the scalar quotient and in a central torus product. Multiplication in the displayed negative-root, torus, positive-root order is an open immersion, hence has unique coordinates: use [lem-sfb-relative-root-product-open-cell] on this rank-one centralizer over each Noetherian local base. The chosen coroot is the diagonal cocharacter, as in step 4. All these are equalities on universal coordinate rings, so the formulas hold on every test algebra and in every residue characteristic. This opposite normalization agrees with [lem-sfb-relative-opposite-root-reflection-map]: direct upper/lower matrix multiplication shows that $x_+(1)x_-(-d)x_+(1)$, for a unit $d$, normalizes the diagonal torus only when $d=1$ (its lower entry is a unit and its diagonal entries are $1-d$). This calculation also holds in the scalar quotient. Thus the reflection node's perfectly paired opposite generator is exactly the one used here.

source.place: Theorem 4.2.6, pp.120-121; rank-one matrix calculation underlying Proposition 6.1.5.

proof.text:
For one of our homomorphisms, write its two normalized opposite-root maps as $u\mapsto c u$, $v\mapsto d v$, with $c,d$ units by step 5. The torus map sends $\alpha^\vee(w)$ to $\beta^\vee(w)$. Apply it to the Gauss identity of step 6 and also use the target Gauss identity, now with parameters $cu,dv$. In
$$R[u,v,(1+uv)^{-1},(1+cd\,uv)^{-1}]$$
uniqueness of the positive coordinate gives $cu/(1+uv)=cu/(1+cd\,uv)$. After clearing denominators this says $c(cd-1)u^2v=0$. The localization of $R[u,v]$ is injective: each inverted factor has constant term $1$ and is therefore a non-zero-divisor, as seen from the least nonzero total degree of a polynomial annihilated by it. Comparing coefficients and cancelling the unit $c$ gives $cd=1$. Thus an agreed positive-root restriction and the agreed torus restriction force an agreed negative-root restriction for two maps. This avoids recovering equality over $R$ from geometric fibres.

source.place: Proposition 6.1.5, proof, pp.189-190; explicit exponent-one Gauss-coordinate comparison.

proof.text:
Let $g,g'$ have the data of the last assertion. Step 5 turns equality on each simple tangent generator into equality on the corresponding entire simple-root subgroup. Step 7 then gives equality on its negative subgroup. For a simple root $\delta$ and a normalized positive generator $X$, [lem-sfb-relative-opposite-root-reflection-map] supplies
$$n_\delta=x_\delta(1)x_{-\delta}(-1)x_\delta(1),$$
which normalizes the source torus and acts by $s_\delta$. Since $g,g'$ agree on both root subgroups, $g(n_\delta)=g'(n_\delta)$. Conjugation by this same source section takes $U_\eta$ to $U_{s_\delta\eta}$: its conjugation of the canonical root parametrization is equivariant for weight $s_\delta\eta$, and its tangent vector is a generator of that weight line, so step 2 gives the identification. Therefore equality on $U_\eta$ implies equality on $U_{s_\delta\eta}$.

Apply [lem-sfb-root-subsystem-simple-orbits] with $V=\mathbf Q\Phi_1\subseteq M_1\otimes\mathbf Q$, $R=\Phi_1$ and $I=\Delta_1$. Restricting the coroot functionals gives the required integral reflection coefficients and reflections preserving the finite reduced root set; the given base spans $V$. It follows that every root is a finite word in the simple reflections applied to a simple root. For a word of length zero equality on that root subgroup is already known; for length $k+1$, apply the conjugation argument of step 8 to the equality obtained for length $k$. Thus $g,g'$ agree on all root subgroups and on $T_1$. The multiplication chart of [lem-sfb-relative-root-product-open-cell] now gives equality on the open cell $C=U^-T_1U^+$. Its root subgroups are the images of our canonical maps: each $u_\eta:\mathbf G_a\simeq U_\eta$ supplied by [lem-sfb-local-split-root-data-weyl-lifts] is a $T_1$-equivariant closed homomorphism of weight $\eta$, so $du_\eta(1)\in\mathfrak g_{1,\eta}$; it is nonzero on the closed fibre because $u_\eta$ stays a closed immersion there, hence generates this free rank-one module over the local ring, and step 2 gives $u_\eta=x_{1,\eta,du_\eta(1)}$.

source.place: Proposition 6.1.13(2), pp.194-195; root-orbit input as in Milne Appendix C.22.

proof.text: The open cell is dense in each geometric fibre: those fibres are connected group schemes locally of finite type, so they equal their identity component and are geometrically irreducible by [lem-sfb-locally-algebraic-group-identity-component], and the cell is a nonempty open containing the identity. Density in residue-field fibres follows as well, since their geometric base-change projections are surjective and open preimages detect nonempty opens. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-fibrewise-dense-open-base-change] to $C\subseteq G_1$. It gives the injection $\mathcal O_{G_1}\hookrightarrow j_*\mathcal O_C$. Because $G_0$ is affine, equality of $g,g'$ on $C$ says that their two pullbacks of each element of its coordinate algebra agree after restriction to $C$; that injection makes the pullbacks equal on $G_1$. The affine morphisms are therefore equal over the Noetherian local base. This also treats empty root sets: then the multiplication chart is $T_1$ and the root assertions are vacuous.

source.place: Proposition 6.1.13(2), final sentence, p.195; relative schematic density, not density only on geometric points.

proof.text: The constructions of step 2 over the Noetherian model $A_0$ and its localizations agree on overlaps by their uniqueness, and step 5 makes the root-map units agree there. The same argument proves local equalities of homomorphisms over $A_0$; equality of morphisms is local on the base. Pull back to $A$. The closed canonical maps and their uniqueness survive this pullback by [lem-sfb-relative-canonical-root-exponential]. The full root-weight and tangent modules are the expected ones by [lem-sfb-arbitrary-base-root-lines-coroots], so the chosen generators and the formula $dg(X)=a_\alpha Y$ have exactly the required meaning over $A$. For any $A\to B$, the root maps are the same base-changed canonical maps, and the polynomial identity becomes $z\mapsto\bar a_\alpha z$; a ring homomorphism preserves units. Differentiation uses the map on dual numbers and hence gives the same scalar. Further base changes compose these formulas. For $B=0$ all group schemes are empty over the empty base and every assertion is the unique corresponding equality. The rigidity assertion over $A$ follows by pulling back the equality over the model, whose two arrows and tangent equalities were descended together in step 1.

split_report.summary: Expanded the exponent-one root-map and pinning-uniqueness argument over arbitrary rings.
